title: Describe the types of requests the team receives in an ordinary week.
evidence: Show a recent sample of incoming requests and how they became known.

title: Identify which work tends to compete for attention at the same time.
evidence: Name a recent day when people were pulled in multiple directions.

title: Follow one recent request from first contact to its final outcome.
evidence: Walk through what actually happened, including any waiting.

title: Ask teammates what they believe must happen before work can be called complete.
evidence: Compare answers from two people doing the work.

title: Identify who needs to talk when a request becomes unclear.
evidence: Describe a recent ambiguity and how it was resolved.

title: Make room for people to describe friction without assigning blame.
evidence: Record one surprising observation raised by a teammate.

title: Name an outcome that matters to the people receiving the service.
evidence: Explain whose experience would improve if this outcome changed.

title: Agree on a shared description for each kind of work the team handles.
evidence: Show examples of work that do and do not fit each description.

title: Discuss what the team will avoid starting when attention is stretched.
evidence: Record a real tradeoff the team agreed to make.

title: Agree on what it means for a request to move to its next step.
evidence: Provide an example of a handoff that met the agreement.

title: Write down the few operating expectations that people ask about most.
evidence: Check whether a newcomer can find and explain these expectations.

title: Agree on a simple way to ask for help when progress stalls.
evidence: Show how a request for assistance was noticed and answered.

title: Set a regular moment to reflect on how the work is going.
evidence: Capture one question the team agreed to revisit.

title: Choose a small set of signals that reveal service experience, not individual productivity.
evidence: Explain how each signal would inform a decision.

title: Keep an up-to-date shared picture of active requests and their current situation.
evidence: Compare the visible picture with real work underway today.

title: Create breathing room before accepting new active work.
evidence: Describe what was finished or deferred to make room.

title: Check aging requests before choosing what to start next.
evidence: Provide a case where an aging request changed a decision.

title: Make exceptions explicit so they do not silently become the normal path.
evidence: Show one exception and who agreed to it.

title: Resolve stuck work through named conversations rather than silent escalation.
evidence: Describe an impediment resolved by coordinated action.

title: Test one small process change for a defined period.
evidence: State what changed, when it was tried, and what people noticed.

title: Review finished work alongside unfinished and aging work.
evidence: Show how both kinds of evidence affected a planning decision.

title: Compare planned work with unexpected demand to uncover recurring surprises.
evidence: Identify a pattern found in recent requests.

title: Use actual completion patterns to discuss realistic near-term commitments.
evidence: Give an example where evidence changed a commitment.

title: Investigate repeated waiting or rework rather than treating each case alone.
evidence: Describe one common source of delay and what was learned.

title: Revisit working agreements when their costs exceed their benefits.
evidence: Show which agreement changed and why.

title: Invite neighboring teams or customers into discussions about recurring friction.
evidence: Describe a conversation that changed how work was coordinated.

title: Review whether an improvement attempt helped, harmed, or made no difference.
evidence: Compare the expected result with what was observed.

title: Discuss tradeoffs between speed, reliability, effort, and customer experience.
evidence: Give a decision where more than one outcome mattered.

title: Adjust how work is made visible as services and demand change.
evidence: Show an example of a new work type being accommodated.

title: Reconsider capacity boundaries when circumstances change, then observe the result.
evidence: Explain the hypothesis and evidence for a capacity change.

title: Coordinate decisions about work across multiple teams without hiding local constraints.
evidence: Trace one cross-team request and the choices it required.

title: Make it clear how operating rules are reviewed and who can propose changes.
evidence: Show a proposed change and how feedback was included.

title: Strengthen the ability to respond together when priorities shift unexpectedly.
evidence: Describe a recent coordinated response and what enabled it.

title: Share useful experiments between teams without forcing the same solution everywhere.
evidence: Document what another team adapted rather than copied.

title: Periodically reconsider which outcomes best represent a useful, sustainable service.
evidence: Explain a signal that was added, removed, or reinterpreted.
